headline: EQX Q2: $861.6M REVENUE IN FIRST COMBINED QUARTER — 1.1M Oz Guidance Set After Orla Merger; Canada Production Up 11% QoQ
snippet: Equinox Gold Corp. (TSX/NYSE: EQX) released Q2 2026 financial results on August 5 — its first earnings report as the combined entity following the July 31 completion of the Orla Mining business combination — posting Q2 revenue of $861.6 million (beating estimates by 10%) while EPS of $0.28 came in slightly below consensus and the stock dipped 0.3% after-hours. Pre-merger Q2 production of 176,836 ounces (including 97,273 oz from Canadian cornerstone mines Greenstone and Valentine, up 11% quarter-on-quarter) was accompanied by combined 2026 guidance of approximately 1.1 million gold equivalent ounces for the merged entity — establishing EQX as North America's second-largest gold producer at a gold price generating record industry margins.

headline: GOLD BOUNCES TO $4,086 ON JOLTS MISS — June Openings Fall To 7.36M vs 7.44M Forecast; September Hike Odds Soften Before Friday NFP
snippet: Gold caught a bid on August 4 as the June JOLTS Job Openings report came in at 7.36 million — below the 7.44 million consensus forecast and down from May's downwardly revised 7.54 million — pushing spot gold up 0.75% to $4,085.80 and partially easing market pricing of a September Federal Reserve rate hike that has capped gold's recovery since the July 9-3 hawkish vote. The JOLTS miss is the first in a sequence of critical labour-market data releases this week culminating in Friday's July Non-Farm Payrolls; analysts have modeled a 150,000+ print as the threshold where September hike odds rise above 60% and gold likely breaks $4,025 support, while a sub-100,000 print — like June's 57,000 surprise — would flip the calculus and could trigger a squeeze toward $4,150.

headline: GOLD ROYALTY POSTS Q2 2026 RESULTS, ACQUIRES TWO NEVADA NSRs For $0.8M — Royalty Streamer Expands US Exposure At $4,000+ Gold
snippet: Gold Royalty Corp. (NYSE American/TSX: GROY) released Q2 2026 financial results on August 5 alongside an announcement of the acquisition of two net smelter return royalties from a private Nevada vendor for US$0.8 million — a portfolio addition in the largest gold-producing US state, expanding the company's royalty footprint at a moment when royalty companies are being revisited by institutional investors as a lower-risk, non-operating form of gold price exposure. The royalty streaming model's immunity to AISC inflation headwinds that are beginning to emerge at producing miners — combined with $4,000+ gold flowing through royalty revenue at 100% margin — is driving renewed focus on the sector as a complement to equity positions in junior explorers.

headline: THE SAME FORCE THAT CRUSHED GOLD ALL YEAR 'HAS FLIPPED' — Iran/Oil Drop Reverses Rate Pressure; Gold Eyes Recovery To $4,150
snippet: GoldSilver.com published analysis in August 2026 arguing that the mechanism that drove gold's correction from its January 2026 record of $5,598 to current levels near $4,086 — oil-driven inflation raising Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations and strengthening the dollar against XAU/USD — has now reversed, as diplomatic pressure to pause US-Iran airstrikes reduces crude prices, which cuts headline CPI, which in turn eases the probability of a September rate hike and removes the primary headwind capping gold's recovery. The piece frames gold's entire 2026 journey in this single macro chain (oil → CPI → Fed rates → dollar → gold) and argues that a sustained Middle East de-escalation scenario provides the cleanest structural tailwind for the junior mining sector, whose NPV assumptions are directly pegged to a long-run gold price that analysts are still revising upward.

headline: CHINA HOLDS JAPAN RARE EARTH EXPORTS AT ZERO — NdPr Stalls At $133.67/kg While MIIT H2 Quota Stays Missing; Market Braces For Catalyst
snippet: China's Rare Earth Industry Association reported an index reading of 267.0 on August 4 as NdPr oxide prices stabilized at $133.67 per kilogram — only marginally above July's benchmark and well short of another leg higher — while separate analysis confirmed that Chinese rare earth exports to Japan have been held at zero for an extended period, extending supply constraints beyond market expectations and forcing Western procurement teams to accelerate diversification agreements with US, Australian, and Canadian producers. The single largest near-term catalyst in the rare earth market remains China's MIIT H2 mining and smelting quota — which should have been published in June or July but has still not appeared as of early August 2026 — leaving the sector in a binary holding pattern where a flat or reduced quota extends the 2026 NdPr price floor, and an upward revision triggers an immediate correction.

headline: COPPER TARIFF VOID: ING Forecasts $6.70/Lb After COMEX-LME Spread Hits 8.4x Historical Average
snippet: ING Think published analysis of the US copper tariff situation arguing that the COMEX-LME spread — which has reached 19.2 cents per pound, approximately 8.4 times its 2005–2025 historical average — reflects sustained market pricing of future tariff risk even though the Commerce Department's June 30 recommended-decision deadline has passed without action from the Trump administration. ING's base case calls for phased refined copper tariffs beginning January 1, 2027 at 15%, which would maintain the COMEX premium structure and support copper prices toward $6.70 per pound (approximately $14,770 per tonne) as US buyers continue front-loading ahead of implementation — a forward price curve directly relevant to every copper developer on the TSX-V and ASX currently preparing updated project economics.

headline: GOLDSEEK SWOT: EVOLUTION MINING'S COPPER PIVOT — ASX Gold Giant's Pipeline Signals Which Projects Acquirers Are Paying For In 2026
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Gold SWOT analysis highlighted Evolution Mining (ASX: EVN) as a case study in how senior Australian gold producers are using record gold margins above A$6,500/oz to aggressively build copper pipeline assets — with Evolution advancing the Northparkes copper-gold joint venture and copper satellite projects alongside its Mungari and Cowal gold operations, explicitly targeting dual-commodity diversification that has been rewarded by generalist fund allocators in the current cycle. For TSX-V and ASX junior investors, Evolution Mining's stated copper acquisition rationale is a leading indicator of what tier-1 and tier-2 producers will pay for: high-grade gold-copper VMS and porphyry systems in stable jurisdictions — the precise geological profile of several of 2025-2026's highest-profile junior exploration programs.

headline: GOLDERA (GERA) BEGINS TSX-V TRADING TODAY — Fancamp Spin-Out Launches With $5.5M Financing And Ontario Exploration Portfolio
snippet: Goldera Inc. (TSX-V: GERA) commenced trading on the TSX Venture Exchange on August 5 following the court-approved spin-out of all of Fancamp Exploration Inc.'s core Ontario mineral exploration assets into the new entity alongside a concurrent $5.5 million private placement, while Fancamp simultaneously renamed itself ERDA Resource Opportunities Inc. (TSX-V: ERDA) and retained its investment issuer structure. The Goldera launch creates a new pure-play Ontario junior exploration vehicle for retail investors — entering a market where TSX-V exploration-stage companies in Tier 1 Canadian mining jurisdictions are attracting renewed deal flow as gold at $4,000+ restores economic viability to projects that were marginal at $1,800 and acquirers compete for advanced-stage Canadian assets.

headline: RENFORTH RESOURCES PARBEC CHANNELS: 8.02 g/t Au Best Hole Near Malartic — Drill Program Now Targeting High-Grade Undercuts
snippet: Renforth Resources Inc. announced surface channel sampling results from the Parbec Gold Deposit in Malartic, Quebec, with eight channels returning highlights including 8.02 g/t gold over 2.55 metres in Channel 58 — with a 0.6-metre sub-interval at 28.77 g/t Au — and 2.97 g/t gold over 10.2 metres in Channel 51 adjacent to the Cadillac Break at the eastern end of the recently stripped open-pit footprint. The Parbec deposit sits in the heart of the Abitibi greenstone belt directly adjacent to Agnico Eagle's Canadian Malartic complex, one of the world's largest gold mines, and the channel results have immediately triggered follow-up diamond drilling targeting undercuts in Channel 51 and Channel 58 — a meaningful step forward for a shallow, open-pittable gold system in a jurisdiction where Agnico Eagle has demonstrated a decade of acquisition interest in neighbouring properties.
